summary: pushgitquickx executes shell commands returned by remote LLM API on push failure
details: The package's `push` subcommand, on any git error, POSTs the git error message and the output of `git status` (branch names, staged/modified/untracked file paths from the installer's working tree) to a hardcoded third-party LLM endpoint (Google Gemini at generativelanguage.googleapis.com, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at router.huggingface.co) using API keys embedded in the source. The JSON response is parsed and every string in its `commandsToRun` array is passed to `execSync` with stdio suppressed, then the push is retried. Command execution is not gated by user confirmation and output is silenced. Any party able to influence the LLM response — the key owner, an operator of the endpoint, or the model itself via prompt-influenced output — can run arbitrary shell commands on the installer's host under the push-error path. The same code path also forwards local repository state (file paths, branch information) to those third-party endpoints without disclosure or opt-in. Two Google API keys are additionally hardcoded as defaults in `analyzeErrorWithAI`.
